chunks: He said: I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying:
Whoever opposes the Book of God and the sunnah of Muhammad (peace be upon him and his family) has indeed disbelieved.

key_terms.خَالَفَ: Opposed/contradicted — active resistance or deliberate contradiction of these two sources
key_terms.سُنَّةَ مُحَمَّدٍ: The Sunnah of Muhammad — the prophetic practice and teachings, the second source of Islamic authority
key_terms.كَفَرَ: Disbelieved — the gravest judgment in Islamic theology, indicating rejection of foundational faith
key_terms.كِتَابَ اللَّهِ: The Book of God — referring to the Quran, the primary source of Islamic law and theology

ai.seo_question: What does Imam Sadiq say about opposing the Quran and the Sunnah of the Prophet?
ai.summary: A companion of Ibn Abi Umayr reports hearing Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq (AS) declare that opposing the Book of God (the Quran) and the Sunnah of the Prophet Muhammad constitutes disbelief (kufr). This hadith, narrated in the chapter on adherence to the Sunnah and the Quran as proofs, establishes the binding authority of both sources. For the early Muslim community, 'disbelieved' (kafara) was a grave declaration, underscoring that the Quran and Sunnah together form an inviolable doctrinal and practical framework.
